elements.quote: Since the onset of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID19), SARS-CoV-2 infection has been circulating globally... The fact that SARS-CoV-2 is still mutating indicates that it remains a global health threat. The WHO study published in Nature [1, 3] also suggested that accurately tracking SARS-CoV-2 and its impact had been challenging.
elements.reason: The introduction describes the global circulation of SARS-CoV-2, the ongoing threat posed by mutations, and the challenge of accurately tracking the virus and its impact, establishing the current state of knowledge and uncertainties.

elements.quote: In addition, the advantage of this study was that compared with the previous meta-analysis of the SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate, first, to avoid the heterogeneous impact of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection definition on SARSCoV-2 reinfection rates... Secondly, considering the heterogeneity of reinfection rates of different variants, we constructed a meta-regression of time-varying reinfection rates... which could provide a basis for subsequent research on prediction of SARS-CoV-2 infection, and could guide significance for the future policy formulation of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection.
elements.reason: The authors explain the need for the review by highlighting the limitations of previous studies (heterogeneity in definitions) and the value of their specific approach (meta-regression of time-varying rates) for policy formulation and future research.

elements.quote: In addition, the advantage of this study was that compared with the previous meta-analysis of the SARSCoV-2 reinfection rate, first, to avoid the heterogeneous impact of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection definition on SARSCoV-2 reinfection rates, so this study defined reinfection and included only literature with reinfection intervals greater than 90 days. Secondly, considering the heterogeneity of reinfection rates of different variants, we constructed a meta-regression of time-varying reinfection rates and compared it with the temporal spline regression without considering heterogeneity
elements.reason: The authors explicitly mention comparing their study to previous meta-analyses, identifying the need for their review based on methodological improvements (defining reinfection intervals and using meta-regression).
This is a systematic review of observational studies (reinfection rates), not a review of intervention effects; therefore, a mechanism of action is not applicable.
This is not a review of complex interventions or delivery contexts; therefore, a logic model is not required.

elements.quote: Therefore, the aim of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to describe and summarize the current reinfection rates in different regions and among diverse populations. Furthermore, the study sought to examine trends in reinfection rates over time, so as to provide reference for the development of global unified reinfection standards and reinfection measures in the future.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the study's objectives regarding the meta-analysis of reinfection rates and the examination of trends over time.
This review is an observational study of reinfection rates, not an intervention effect study, therefore PICO is not required.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) Conformed to research questions, i.e., studies that estimated the reinfection rate of SARS-CoV-2 or we could calculate it based on the data provided in the paper; (2) The study design included cohort study, case-control study, and descriptive study; (3) The study fited our working definition of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection... The exclusion criteria were: (1) The sample size was less than 20; (2) Belonged to one of the following types of studies: editorial, case report, case series study, systematic review, meta-analysis, animal experiment, news report; (3) Secondary reporting or articles on repeated studies of the same population; (4) Grey literature
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists inclusion and exclusion criteria, including study designs (cohort, case-control, descriptive) and specific definitions for reinfection.
